verses.zh: 禍 哉 ！ 你 這 毀 滅 人 的 ， 自 己 倒 不 被 毀 滅 ； 行 事 詭 詐 的 ， 人 倒 不 以 詭 詐 待 你 。 你 毀 滅 罷 休 了 ， 自 己 必 被 毀 滅 ； 你 行 完 了 詭 詐 ， 人 必 以 詭 詐 待 你 。
verses.en: The destroyer is as good as dead,[NOTE:1] you who have not been destroyed!The deceitful one is as good as dead,[NOTE:2] the one whom others have not deceived!When you are through destroying, you will be destroyed;when you finish[NOTE:3] deceiving, others will deceive you!
notes: Heb “Woe [to] the destroyer.”sn In this context “the destroyer” appears to refer collectively to the hostile nations (vv. 3-4). Assyria would probably have been primary in the minds of the prophet and his audience.
Heb “and the deceitful one”; NAB, NIV84 “O traitor”; NIV11 “you betrayer”; NRSV “you treacherous one.” In the parallel structure הוֹי (hoy, “woe [to]”) does double duty.

The form in the Hebrew text appears to derive from an otherwise unattested verb נָלָה (nalah). The translation follows the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa in reading ככלתך, a Piel infinitival form from the verbal root כָּלָה (kalah), meaning “finish.”

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 求 你 施 恩 於 我 們 ； 我 們 等 候 你 。 求 你 每 早 晨 作 我 們 的 膀 臂 ， 遭 難 的 時 候 為 我 們 的 拯 救 。
verses.en: Lord, be merciful to us! We wait for you.Give us strength each morning.[NOTE:1] Deliver us when distress comes.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Be their arm each morning.” “Arm” is a symbol for strength. The mem suffixed to the noun has been traditionally understood as a third person suffix, but this is contrary to the context, where the people speak of themselves in the first person. The mem (מ) is probably enclitic with ellipsis of the pronoun, which can be supplied from the context. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:589, n. 1.
Heb “[Be] also our deliverance in the time of distress.”

verses.zh: 喧 嚷 的 響 聲 一 發 ， 眾 民 奔 逃 ； 你 一 興 起 ， 列 國 四 散 。
verses.en: The nations run away when they hear a loud noise;[NOTE:1] the nations scatter when you spring into action![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “at the sound of tumult the nations run away.”
Heb “because of your exaltation the nations scatter.”

verses.zh: 你 們 所 擄 的 必 被 斂 盡 ， 好 像 螞 蚱 吃 （ 原 文 是 斂 ） 盡 禾 稼 。 人 要 蹦 在 其 上 ， 好 像 蝗 蟲 一 樣 。
verses.en: Your plunder[NOTE:1] disappears as if locusts were eating it;[NOTE:2] they swarm over it like locusts.[NOTE:3]
notes: The pronoun is plural; the statement is addressed to the nations who have stockpiled plunder from their conquests of others.
Heb “and your plunder is gathered, the gathering of the locust.”
Heb “like a swarm of locusts swarming on it.”

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 被 尊 崇 ， 因 他 居 在 高 處 ； 他 以 公 平 公 義 充 滿 錫 安 。
verses.en: The Lord is exalted,[NOTE:1] indeed,[NOTE:2] he lives in heaven;[NOTE:3] he fills Zion with justice and fairness.
notes: Or “elevated”; NCV, NLT “is very great.”
Or “for” (KJV, NASB, NIV).
Heb “on high” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); CEV “in the heavens.”

verses.zh: 你 一 生 一 世 必 得 安 穩 ─ 有 豐 盛 的 救 恩 ， 並 智 慧 和 知 識 ； 你 以 敬 畏 耶 和 華 為 至 寶 。
verses.en: He is your constant source of stability;[NOTE:1] he abundantly provides safety and great wisdom;[NOTE:2] he gives all this to those who fear him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and he is the stability of your times.”
Heb “a rich store of deliverance, wisdom, and knowledge.”
Heb “the fear of the Lord, it is his treasure.”

verses.zh: 看 哪 ， 他 們 的 豪 傑 在 外 頭 哀 號 ； 求 和 的 使 臣 痛 痛 哭 泣 。
verses.en: Look, ambassadors[NOTE:1] cry out in the streets;messengers sent to make peace[NOTE:2] weep bitterly.
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew word is unknown. Proposals include “heroes” (cf. KJV, ASV “valiant ones”; NASB, NIV “brave men”); “priests,” “residents [of Jerusalem].” The present translation assumes that the term is synonymous with “messengers of peace,” with which it corresponds in the parallel structure of the verse.
Heb “messengers of peace,” apparently those responsible for negotiating the agreements that have been broken (see v. 8).

verses.zh: 大 路 荒 涼 ， 行 人 止 息 ； 敵 人 背 約 ， 藐 視 城 邑 ， 不 顧 人 民 。
verses.en: Highways are empty;[NOTE:1] there are no travelers.[NOTE:2] Treaties are broken;[NOTE:3] witnesses are despised;[NOTE:4] human life is treated with disrespect.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “desolate” (NAB, NASB); NIV, NRSV, NLT “deserted.”
Heb “the one passing by on the road ceases.”
Heb “one breaks a treaty”; NAB “Covenants are broken.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “he despises cities.” The term עָרִים (ʿarim, “cities”) probably needs to be emended to an original עֵדִים (ʿedim, “[legal] witnesses”), a reading that is preserved in the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa. Confusion of dalet (ד) and resh (ר) is a well-attested scribal error.
Heb “he does not regard human beings.”

verses.zh: 地 上 悲 哀 衰 殘 ； 利 巴 嫩 羞 愧 枯 乾 ； 沙 崙 像 曠 野 ； 巴 珊 和 迦 密 的 樹 林 凋 殘 。
verses.en: The land[NOTE:1] dries up[NOTE:2] and withers away;the forest of Lebanon shrivels up[NOTE:3] and decays.Sharon[NOTE:4] is like the arid rift valley;[NOTE:5] Bashan and Carmel[NOTE:6] are parched.[NOTE:7]
notes: Or “earth” (KJV); NAB “the country.”
Or “mourns” (BDB 5 s.v. I אָבַל). HALOT 6-7 lists homonyms I אבל (“mourn”) and II אבל (“dry up”). They propose the second here on the basis of parallelism. See 24:4.
Heb “Lebanon is ashamed.” The Hiphil is exhibitive, expressing the idea, “exhibits shame.” In this context the statement alludes to the withering of vegetation.
Sharon was a fertile plain along the Mediterranean coast. See 35:2.

The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) is a geographic feature extending from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba. Especially in the vicinity of the Dead Sea and then ranging southward, it is very dry with little vegetation.
Both of these areas were known for their trees and vegetation. See 2:13; 35:2.
Heb “shake off [their leaves]” (so ASV, NRSV); NAB “are stripped bare.”

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 說 ： 現 在 我 要 起 來 ； 我 要 興 起 ； 我 要 勃 然 而 興 。
verses.en: “Now I will rise up,” says the Lord.“Now I will exalt myself;now I will magnify myself.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “lift myself up” (KJV); NLT “show my power and might.”

verses.zh: 你 們 要 懷 的 是 糠 秕 ， 要 生 的 是 碎 秸 ； 你 們 的 氣 就 是 吞 滅 自 己 的 火 。
verses.en: You conceive straw,[NOTE:1] you give birth to chaff;your breath is a fire that destroys you.[NOTE:2]
notes: The second person verb and pronominal forms in this verse are plural. The hostile nations are the addressed, as the next verse makes clear.
The hostile nations’ plans to destroy God’s people will come to nothing; their hostility will end up being self-destructive.

verses.zh: 列 邦 必 像 已 燒 的 石 灰 ， 像 已 割 的 荊 棘 在 火 中 焚 燒 。
verses.en: The nations will be burned to ashes;[NOTE:1] like thornbushes that have been cut down, they will be set on fire.
notes: Heb “will be a burning to lime.” See Amos 2:1.

verses.zh: 你 們 遠 方 的 人 當 聽 我 所 行 的 ； 你 們 近 處 的 人 當 承 認 我 的 大 能 。
verses.en: You who are far away, listen to what I have done!You who are close by, recognize my strength.”

verses.zh: 錫 安 中 的 罪 人 都 懼 怕 ； 不 敬 虔 的 人 被 戰 兢 抓 住 。 我 們 中 間 誰 能 與 吞 滅 的 火 同 住 ？ 我 們 中 間 誰 能 與 永 火 同 住 呢 ？
verses.en: Sinners are afraid in Zion;panic[NOTE:1] grips the godless.[NOTE:2] They say,[NOTE:3] “Who among us can coexist with destructive fire?Who among us can coexist with unquenchable[NOTE:4] fire?”
notes: Or “trembling” (ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “shake with fear.”
Or “the defiled”; TEV “The sinful people of Zion”; NLT “The sinners in Jerusalem.”
The words “they say” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Or “perpetual”; or “everlasting” (KJV, ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 行 事 公 義 、 說 話 正 直 、 憎 惡 欺 壓 的 財 利 、 擺 手 不 受 賄 賂 、 塞 耳 不 聽 流 血 的 話 ， 閉 眼 不 看 邪 惡 事 的 ，
verses.en: The one who lives[NOTE:1] uprightly[NOTE:2] and speaks honestly,the one who refuses to profit from oppressive measuresand rejects a bribe,[NOTE:3] the one who does not plot violent crimes[NOTE:4] and does not seek to harm others[NOTE:5]—
notes: Heb “walks” (so NASB, NIV).
Or, possibly, “justly”; NAB “who practices virtue.”
Heb “[who] shakes off his hands from grabbing hold of a bribe.”
Heb “[who] shuts his ear from listening to bloodshed.”
Heb “[who] closes his eyes from seeing evil.”

verses.zh: 他 必 居 高 處 ； 他 的 保 障 是 磐 石 的 堅 壘 ； 他 的 糧 必 不 缺 乏 （ 原 文 是 賜 給 ） ； 他 的 水 必 不 斷 絕 。
verses.en: this is the person who will live in a secure place;[NOTE:1] he will find safety in the rocky, mountain strongholds;[NOTE:2] he will have foodand a constant supply of water.
notes: Heb “he [in the] exalted places will live.”
Heb “mountain strongholds, cliffs [will be] his elevated place.”

verses.zh: 你 的 眼 必 見 王 的 榮 美 ， 必 見 遼 闊 之 地 。
verses.en: You will see a king in his splendor;[NOTE:1] you will see a wide land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your eyes will see a king in his beauty”; NIV, NRSV “the king.”
Heb “a land of distances,” i.e., an extensive land.

verses.zh: 你 的 心 必 思 想 那 驚 嚇 的 事 ， 自 問 說 ： 記 數 目 的 在 哪 裡 呢 ？ 平 貢 銀 的 在 哪 裡 呢 ？ 數 戍 樓 的 在 哪 裡 呢 ？
verses.en: Your mind will recall the terror you experienced,[NOTE:1] and you will ask yourselves,[NOTE:2] “Where is the scribe?Where is the one who weighs the money?Where is the one who counts the towers?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “your heart will meditate on terror.”
The words “and you will ask yourselves” are supplied in the translation for clarification and stylistic reasons.
The people refer to various Assyrian officials who were responsible for determining the amount of taxation or tribute Judah must pay to the Assyrian king.

verses.zh: 你 必 不 見 那 強 暴 的 民 ， 就 是 說 話 深 奧 ， 你 不 能 明 白 ， 言 語 呢 喃 ， 你 不 能 懂 得 的 。
verses.en: You will no longer see a defiant[NOTE:1] peoplewhose language you do not comprehend,[NOTE:2] whose derisive speech you do not understand.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew form נוֹעָז (noʿaz) is a Niphal participle derived from יָעַז (yaʿaz, an otherwise unattested verb) or from עָזָז (ʿazaz, “be strong,” unattested elsewhere in the Niphal). Some prefer to emend the form to לוֹעֵז (loʿez) which occurs in Ps 114:1 with the meaning “speak a foreign language.” See HALOT 809 s.v. עזז, 533 s.v. לעז. In this case, one might translate “people who speak a foreign language.”
Heb “a people too deep of lip to hear.” The phrase “deep of lip” must be an idiom meaning “lips that speak words that are unfathomable [i.e., incomprehensible].”
Heb “derision of tongue there is no understanding.” The Niphal of לָעַג (laʿag) occurs only here. In the Qal and Hiphil the verb means “to deride, mock.” A related noun is used in 28:11.

verses.zh: 你 要 看 錫 安 ─ 我 們 守 聖 節 的 城 ！ 你 的 眼 必 見 耶 路 撒 冷 為 安 靜 的 居 所 ， 為 不 挪 移 的 帳 幕 ， 橛 子 永 不 拔 出 ， 繩 索 一 根 也 不 折 斷 。
verses.en: Look at Zion, the city where we hold religious festivals!You[NOTE:1] will see Jerusalem,[NOTE:2] a peaceful settlement,a tent that stays put;[NOTE:3] its stakes will never be pulled up;none of its ropes will snap in two.
notes: Heb “your eyes” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Or “that does not travel”; NASB “which shall not be folded.”

verses.zh: 在 那 裡 ， 耶 和 華 必 顯 威 嚴 與 我 們 同 在 ， 當 作 江 河 寬 闊 之 地 ； 其 中 必 沒 有 盪 槳 搖 櫓 的 船 來 往 ， 也 沒 有 威 武 的 船 經 過 。
verses.en: Instead the Lord will rule there as our mighty king.[NOTE:1] Rivers and wide streams will flow through it;[NOTE:2] no war galley will enter;[NOTE:3] no large ships will sail through.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “But there [as] a mighty one [will be] the Lord for us.”
Heb “a place of rivers, streams wide of hands [i.e., on both sides].”
Heb “a ship of rowing will not go into it.”
Heb “and a mighty ship will not pass through it.”

verses.zh: 因 為 ， 耶 和 華 是 審 判 我 們 的 ； 耶 和 華 是 給 我 們 設 律 法 的 ； 耶 和 華 是 我 們 的 王 ； 他 必 拯 救 我 們 。
verses.en: For the Lord, our ruler,the Lord, our commander,the Lord, our king—he will deliver us.

verses.zh: 你 的 繩 索 鬆 開 ： 不 能 栽 穩 桅 杆 ， 也 不 能 揚 起 篷 來 。 那 時 許 多 擄 來 的 物 被 分 了 ； 瘸 腿 的 把 掠 物 奪 去 了 。
verses.en: Though at this time your ropes are slack,[NOTE:1] the mast is not secured,[NOTE:2] and the sail[NOTE:3] is not unfurled,at that time you will divide up a great quantity of loot;[NOTE:4] even the lame will drag off plunder.[NOTE:5]
notes: The words “though at this time” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The first half of the verse is addressed to Judah and contrasts the nation’s present weakness with its future prosperity. Judah is compared to a ship that is incapable of sailing.
Heb “they do not fasten the base of their mast.” On כֵּן (ken, “base”) see BDB 487 s.v. III כֵּן and HALOT 483 s.v. III כֵּן.
Or perhaps, “flag.”
Heb “then there will be divided up loot of plunder [in] abundance.”
Judah’s victory over its enemies will be so thorough there will be more than enough plunder for everyone, even slow-moving lame men who would normally get left out in the rush to gather the loot.

verses.zh: 城 內 居 民 必 不 說 ： 我 病 了 ； 其 中 居 住 的 百 姓 ， 罪 孽 都 赦 免 了 。
verses.en: No resident of Zion[NOTE:1] will say, “I am ill”;the people who live there will have their sin forgiven.
notes: The words “of Zion” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
